title: SBA 7(a) and 504 loan packaging checklist for brokers
summary: An SBA loan packaging checklist for brokers: the 7(a) and 504 forms, the eligibility checks lenders run, every document SOP 50 10 8.1 names, and why packages stall.
body_markdown:
You know the call. A borrower with a good business wants $1.2 million to buy the building they lease and refinance some equipment debt. You have tax returns from last spring, a profit and loss statement the bookkeeper exported last week, and a promise that the personal financial statement is “almost done”.


Whether that file moves in days or sits for weeks depends less on the deal than on the package. Lenders and CDCs read an SBA file against a fixed list, set by SBA’s Standard Operating Procedure 50 10. The current version, SOP 50 10 8.1, took effect on October 1, 2026.\[1,9\] A package that answers that list in order gets read. One that makes the lender ask for things goes to the bottom of the pile.


This guide is that list, written for the person putting the file together. Every SBA-specific item is cited to SBA’s own procedures or forms. Kita also keeps a sourced reference to each program, at[SBA 7(a)](https://www.kita.ai/lending-programs/sba-7a) ,[SBA 504](https://www.kita.ai/lending-programs/sba-504) ,[SBA Express](https://www.kita.ai/lending-programs/sba-express) and the rest of the[lending programs hub](https://www.kita.ai/lending-programs) .


Quick answer


A complete SBA package gives the lender everything SBA’s procedures make it check: a borrower information form (SBA Form 1919 for 7(a), SBA Form 1244 for 504), a personal financial statement for every owner of 20% or more, three years of business financials plus a recent interim, a debt schedule, affiliates’ statements, an IRS transcript authorization, and the documents behind every dollar of the use of proceeds and the equity injection.\[7,9\]


The rules are in SBA’s SOP 50 10 8.1, in effect since October 1, 2026. The checklists below follow it item by item.


Key takeaways


-


A 7(a) package goes to one lender on SBA Form 1919. A 504 package goes to a Certified Development Company on SBA Form 1244 and needs a Third Party Lender’s written commitment as well.


-


Screen eligibility first: size with affiliates, business type, 100% of ownership and the citizenship rule, prior government losses, filed tax returns, and for 504 the fixed-asset, occupancy and jobs tests.


-


The core of both packages is the same: owner financial statements within 90 days, three years of business financials, an interim within 120 days, a full debt schedule, affiliates’ statements and an IRS transcript authorization.


-


Most stalls are avoidable: stale dates, numbers that do not match the transcripts, ownership that does not add up, unsupported add-backs and equity that cannot be traced.


01


## Who reads an SBA package, and what they need from it


A 7(a) loan is made by a participating lender, and SBA guarantees part of it. A Standard 7(a) loan is anything above $350,000 up to $5,000,000. Loans of $350,000 or less are 7(a) Small loans, and SBA Express is a separate streamlined route; both ask for less paper.\[5,9\] The lender either sends the file to SBA’s loan guaranty processing center, where SBA decides eligibility and credit, or approves it under its own delegated authority (the Preferred Lenders Program), in which case SBA does not review the credit before it issues a loan number.\[5\]


A 504 loan is different in kind. It finances fixed assets, and three parties fund the project: a private Third Party Lender, a Certified Development Company whose share is funded by a debenture SBA guarantees, and the borrower.\[7,16\] Only CDCs make 504 loans, so your package goes to the CDC, and the Third Party Lender has to be committed in writing before the application goes in.\[7,16\]


### Where a package goes after it leaves you


Your package is the input to someone else’s credit memo. The 7(a) and 504 paths have different readers.


7(a)


1.


You and the borrower


SBA Form 1919, financials, owner statements, use-of-proceeds documents


2.


7(a) lender


Credit memo, credit reports, IRS transcripts, its own credit decision


3.


SBA


Non-delegated: SBA reviews eligibility and credit. Delegated (PLP): the lender approves and SBA issues a loan number


504


1.


You and the borrower


SBA Form 1244 inputs, project costs, financials, owner statements


2.


CDC and Third Party Lender


The CDC writes the credit memo; the Third Party Lender commits to the senior loan in writing


3.


SBA


All 504 loans are processed at SBA’s Sacramento Loan Processing Center


Simplified from SOP 50 10 8.1, Section B, Chapter 1, Appendix 20 and Section C, Chapter 1. The lender or CDC decides what to ask for beyond SBA’s minimum.


Either way, your package becomes the raw material for someone else’s credit memo, and it should answer that memo’s questions before they are asked.\[5,7\]


### The standard 504 project, by source of funds


Three parties fund one project, so a 504 package has to satisfy a CDC and a bank at the same time.


50%


40%


10%


-


Third Party Lender


50% or more, senior lien


-


CDC / SBA debenture


Up to 40%, guaranteed 100% by SBA


-


Borrower


At least 10%


The standard structure from SOP 50 10 8.1, Section C, Chapter 1. The borrower’s share rises to 15% for a new business or a limited or special purpose property, and to 20% when both apply.


02


## Packaging an SBA loan, in six steps


The order matters. Collecting three years of financials for a borrower who fails the ownership rule is wasted work for everyone.


1. 01


Screen eligibility before you collect anything


Confirm the business is an operating, for-profit U.S. business that is small under SBA size standards with its affiliates, is not an ineligible type, and that every direct and indirect owner and required guarantor is a U.S. citizen or U.S. national living in the United States.\[1,14\]


2. 02


Match the use of proceeds to the program


A 504 loan finances fixed assets such as land, buildings and long-life equipment, and cannot fund working capital or inventory. A 7(a) loan covers a wider range of uses, including working capital, equipment, real estate, refinancing and business acquisitions.\[5,16\]


3. 03


Map the ownership and the guarantors


List 100% of direct and indirect ownership. Every owner of 20% or more provides a personal financial statement and an unlimited full guaranty, and their spouse’s and minor children’s holdings are combined with theirs.\[1,4,9\]


4. 04


Collect the financials for every period and every entity


Three years of business statements or tax returns, an interim statement dated within 120 days of submission, a detailed debt schedule, the same for each affiliate, and a signed IRS Form 4506-C or 8821 so the lender can pull transcripts.\[4,9\]


5. 05


Document the uses of proceeds and the equity injection


Quotes, purchase agreements, leases, appraisals and cost breakdowns for what the loan buys, and bank records that trace the borrower’s cash injection from its source account to the business.\[6,7,9\]


6. 06


Check dates and consistency, then disclose your role


Make sure nothing has gone stale, that the numbers agree across the forms, statements and returns, and that your involvement as an agent is recorded on SBA Form 159 for the lender or CDC.\[3,9\]


03


## The eligibility checks lenders run first


These are pass-or-fail. No amount of collateral or cash flow fixes a business that is too large, the wrong type, or owned by someone SBA cannot lend to. The 7(a) program page lists the basics: an operating, for-profit, U.S. business that is small under SBA size standards, not an ineligible type, creditworthy, and unable to get the credit on reasonable terms elsewhere.\[15\]


SBA eligibility checks and what to collect for each What the lender checks What to have ready Applies to


Operating, for-profit business located in the United States Formation documents (bylaws, partnership or operating agreement) and tax returns\[1,15\] 7(a) and 504


Small under SBA size standards, counting affiliates Affiliates and their financials, and which test applies: the industry size standard, or the alternative (tangible net worth up to $20 million and average net income after federal taxes up to $6.5 million over the prior two fiscal years)\[1\] 7(a) and 504


Not an ineligible type of business A plain description of what the business does. Lending, passive and speculative businesses are among the types SBA excludes\[1\] 7(a) and 504


Every owner and required guarantor is a U.S. citizen or U.S. national with a principal residence in the United States An ownership chart that adds up to 100%, direct and indirect, and evidence of status for any U.S. national. Entity owners must be organized in the United States\[1,14\] 7(a) and 504


No prior loss to the government and no delinquent federal debt A schedule of any previous government financing for the business, its affiliates and its principals\[1,7\] 7(a) and 504


Required federal tax returns have been filed A signed IRS Form 4506-C or Form 8821 so the lender can obtain transcripts\[4\] 7(a) and 504


A franchise brand is on the SBA Franchise Directory The brand name and agreement, plus any management agreement that sits outside the franchise disclosure documents\[1,9\] 7(a) and 504


Credit is not available elsewhere on reasonable terms The facts behind the request. The lender certifies this and explains it in the credit memo\[1\] 7(a) and 504


The project is fixed assets, not working capital Land, buildings, or machinery and equipment with a remaining useful life of at least 10 years. Working capital and inventory are not eligible\[16\] 504


The business will occupy enough of the property At least 51% of an existing building, or 60% of new construction\[2\] 504


The project creates or retains jobs, or meets a public policy goal Current headcount and jobs created or retained: one job per $95,000 SBA guarantees, or one per $150,000 for small manufacturers and energy public policy projects\[7\] 504


Two rules catch brokers most often. The first is ownership: since March 1, 2026, lawful permanent residents cannot own any part of the business, and an ineligible owner in the six months before the loan number is issued makes the business ineligible unless they fully divest first.\[1,14\]


The second is affiliation. Size is measured with every affiliate counted as one business, and SBA’s loan limits apply the same way, so the lender has to identify affiliates and document them in its analysis.\[1,5\] Ask about other businesses the owners control at the first meeting, not after the package is built.


04


## The SBA forms in a 7(a) or 504 package


SBA’s forms are fewer than most borrowers expect. Much of the package is the borrower’s own financial records. These are the forms you will meet, and who completes each one.


The SBA and IRS forms in a 7(a) or 504 package Form What it is Program Who completes or signs it


SBA Form 1919 Borrower Information Form: the applicant, its owners, the loan request and its purposes, existing debt and prior government financing 7(a) The applicant business, one per co-borrower. The purpose amounts across all of them should add up to the loan request\[9,10\]


SBA Form 1244 Application for Section 504 Loan (504 Borrower Information Form), with 100% of ownership disclosed 504 The borrower as applicant and the CDC as lender\[7,11\]


SBA Form 413 Personal Financial Statement 7(a) and 504 Each owner of 20% or more and each guarantor other than a supplemental guarantor, signed and dated within 90 days. Lenders and CDCs may use their own equivalent\[7,9,12\]


IRS Form 4506-C or Form 8821 IRS authorizations that let the lender obtain tax return transcripts 7(a) and 504 The applicant signs. On Form 8821 the lender is the designee; SBA does not allow the borrower or its own tax preparer to file it\[4\]


SBA Form 159 Fee Disclosure and Compensation Agreement 7(a) and 504 The applicant, the agent and the lender or CDC, one form for each agent. Generated in the SBA loan system\[3,13\]


SBA Form 148 or 148L Unconditional Guarantee, or Unconditional Limited Guarantee 7(a) and 504 Each owner of 20% or more gives an unlimited full guaranty. 7(a) lenders may use their own equivalent form\[4,6\]


SBA Form 155 Standby Creditor’s Agreement, for debt on full standby that counts toward equity 7(a) The standby creditor, with a copy of the note attached. Lenders may use their own equivalent\[5\]


SBA Form 2481 Historic Property Borrower Certification 504, if applicable The borrower\[7\]


SBA Forms 1050 and 722 Settlement Sheet (use of proceeds) and the Equal Employment Opportunity poster 7(a), at closing The lender and borrower. Form 1050 is not used for 7(a) Small, SBA Express or Export Express loans\[6\]


05


## The SBA 7(a) package checklist


Appendix 20 of the SOP consolidates what every 7(a) loan file must contain, whatever the processing method.\[9\] The checklist below follows it. The lender may still ask for anything else it needs to make a credit decision, and for 7(a) Small and SBA Express loans some of the use-of-proceeds detail is needed only to the extent it supports the uses and the credit analysis.\[9\]


SBA 7(a) checklist


Borrower and owners


-


SBA Form 1919 for the applicant and for each co-borrower, signed by an authorized representative\[9\]


-


Ownership chart showing 100% of direct and indirect owners\[9\]


-


Personal financial statement (SBA Form 413 or the lender’s form) for every owner of 20% or more, including the assets of a spouse and minor children, and for each proposed guarantor, dated within 90 days of submission\[9\]


-


Evidence of status (birth certificate or passport) for any owner who is a U.S. national\[9\]


Business financials


-


Business financial statements or tax returns for the last 3 years: year-end balance sheets with a detailed debt schedule, and year-end profit and loss statements\[9\]


-


Interim balance sheet with a detailed debt schedule, and an interim profit and loss statement, dated within 120 days of submission\[9\]


-


The same statements for every affiliate\[9\]


-


Signed IRS Form 4506-C or Form 8821 for tax transcripts\[4,6\]


-


Start-ups and new businesses: detailed projections with assumptions that show debt service coverage of at least 1.15 within 2 years of funding\[9\]


Uses of proceeds and collateral


-


Copy of the lease, if there is one\[9\]


-


Itemized machinery and equipment to be bought, with cost quotes\[9\]


-


A list of every asset the loan will buy, and a list of all collateral\[9\]


-


Management agreement, if the business will be run under one\[9\]


If the loan buys real estate


-


Appraisal, signed purchase agreement, the lender’s environmental questionnaire if applicable, and a cost breakdown for any improvements\[9\]


If the loan buys a business


-


Buy-sell or purchase agreement, and a pro forma balance sheet for the business as of the date of transfer\[9\]


-


A business valuation meeting Appendix 15. It must be requested by and prepared for the lender; one prepared for the buyer or seller cannot be used\[8,9\]


-


Seller’s financial statements for the last 3 fiscal years, plus an interim no older than 120 days, dated and signed or certified by the seller\[9\]


If the loan refinances debt


-


Copies of each note and security agreement being refinanced, and 12 months of transcripts or statements showing the debt is current\[9\]


Equity injection


-


For cash: the check or wire with proof it cleared into the borrower’s account or escrow, at least 30 days of statements from the source account, and proof of deposit or a settlement statement. A gift letter or promissory note alone is not enough\[6\]


-


For debt counted as equity: a standby agreement on full standby, with the note attached\[5\]


Your role


-


SBA Form 159, completed and signed by you, the applicant and the lender\[3\]


### What the credit memo will ask of your numbers


The documents get a file read. The numbers decide what happens next, and SBA tells the lender exactly what to test. Cash flow is the primary source of repayment, and if the analysis does not show reasonable assurance of repayment from it, the loan must be declined whatever the collateral.\[5\] Package with these in mind:


-


**Debt service coverage of at least 1.15** on a historical or projected basis, and 1:1 on a global basis, counting principal and interest on all business debt including the new loan.\[5\]


-


**Projections when history falls short.** If the last full year and the interim do not show enough coverage, the lender needs two years of detailed projections with the assumptions behind them.\[5\]


-


**Support for every adjustment to cash flow,** such as owner’s draw, rent, non-recurring income, unfunded capital spending and distributions for S-corporation taxes.\[5\]


-


**A reason for heavy working capital.** When half or more of the proceeds are working capital, the lender has to explain why that level is necessary for the business.\[5\]


-


**The equity position and its source.** Start-ups (operating a year or less) need an injection of at least 10% of project cost, and only certain sources count, such as unborrowed cash, qualifying gifts and debt on full standby.\[5\] Changes of ownership have their own rules in Appendix 15.\[8\]


06


## The SBA 504 application checklist


The CDC assembles the 504 application and keeps the full file, but most of what goes into it comes from the borrower, and through you.\[7\] Before you start, confirm the project fits: land, buildings, or machinery and equipment with at least ten years of remaining useful life. Working capital and inventory are not eligible uses.\[16\]


SBA 504 checklist


Application and project


-


SBA Form 1244, with 100% of direct and indirect ownership listed\[7\]


-


Key cost documents: contractor costs and estimates, equipment vendor quotes, an itemized list of professional fees, and full or partly executed purchase agreements\[7\]


-


Independent appraisal of the project real estate, where required\[7\]


-


Environmental analysis if applicable, and SBA Form 2481 for a historic property\[7\]


-


A letter of intent or term sheet from the Third Party Lender that states its terms and why it will not finance the whole project\[7\]


Owners and guarantors


-


SBA Form 413 (or the CDC’s form) signed and dated within 90 days, and one year of personal federal tax returns, for each owner of 20% or more and each proposed guarantor\[7\]


-


Evidence of status for any owner who is a U.S. national\[7\]


Business financials


-


Balance sheets, income statements and tax returns for 3 years, or 2 years if the business qualifies under the alternative size standard\[7\]


-


Interim balance sheet and income statement dated within 120 days of submission, with accounts receivable and payable agings\[7\]


-


Projected income statements for the first 2 years after closing where appropriate. A new business also needs a pro forma balance sheet and a monthly cash flow for 12 months or until 3 months past breakeven, whichever is longer\[7\]


-


Schedule of business debts: original date and amount, payment, status, rate, balance, maturity, creditor and collateral\[7\]


-


Schedule of any previous government financing for the business, its affiliates and principals\[7\]


-


Names of affiliates, with their last 2 years of statements or returns (3 under the industry size standard)\[7\]


-


Signed IRS Form 4506-C or Form 8821\[7\]


If the project refinances debt


-


Current debt and lien instruments, transcripts of account for each debt, and the refinancing certifications\[7\]


Your role


-


SBA Form 159, completed and signed by you, the applicant and the CDC\[3,7\]


The CDC also obtains credit reports dated within 90 days for the applicant, owners of 20% or more, affiliates and guarantors, and for projects of $5,000,000 or more it needs the Third Party Lender’s own underwriting analysis.\[7\] The CDC’s credit memo tests historical debt service coverage of at least 1.15, using the last fiscal year or the average of the last two.\[7\]


07


## Why SBA packages stall


An incomplete package tends to slow down rather than fail outright: a lender emails for the missing piece, and while it waits the clock runs on every dated document in the file. These are the patterns behind most of those emails.


1. 01


Documents that went stale


Personal financial statements must be dated within 90 days and interim business statements within 120 days of submission. A file that waits a month for one missing item can come back needing new versions of both.\[7,9\]


2. 02


Numbers that do not match the tax transcripts


The lender has to reconcile the financials against IRS transcripts. A business that has not filed its required returns is not eligible, and if the IRS has no record of a required year the loan cannot be disbursed until it is resolved.\[4\]


3. 03


Ownership that does not add up


The ownership entered for SBA has to total 100%, direct and indirect, and one ineligible owner or guarantor makes the whole business ineligible unless they fully divest before the loan number is issued.\[1,9\]


4. 04


A debt schedule with gaps


Debt service is measured on all business debt including the new loan, and the lender needs a current schedule that includes any shareholder debt. A loan the owner forgot to mention changes the coverage.\[5\]


5. 05


Add-backs with nothing behind them


The credit memo has to justify each addition or subtraction to cash flow, such as owner’s draw, rent, non-recurring income and distributions for S-corporation taxes. Send the support with the add-back.\[5\]


6. 06


An equity injection nobody can trace


A gift letter or promissory note does not prove a cash injection on its own; the lender needs bank records that follow the money. Fees paid to an agent do not count toward equity.\[5,6\]


7. 07


An acquisition valuation ordered by the wrong party


For a change of ownership the valuation must be requested by and prepared for the lender. A valuation the buyer or seller commissioned cannot be used, however good it is.\[8\]


8. 08


A 504 file without a committed Third Party Lender


The application needs the Third Party Lender’s letter of intent or term sheet, including why it will not finance the whole project, and the cost documents that support the project budget.\[7\]


A simple habit catches most of them: before you send a file, put the dates of every dated document on one line, and tie the revenue on the tax returns, the year-end statements and Form 1919 to each other. If you cannot make them agree, the lender will not either.


08


## SBA’s rules for brokers and packagers


SBA has a name for you. Its regulations define an Agent as an authorized representative, including a packager or consultant, who conducts business with SBA for an applicant or lender. A Packager is an Agent paid by the applicant or the lender to prepare the application, and a Referral Agent is one who refers an applicant to a lender or the reverse.\[3\]


Three of the rules that follow from that matter for every package:


-


**Disclose on SBA Form 159.** For an agent who is not a lender service provider under an SBA-reviewed agreement, Form 159, the Fee Disclosure and Compensation Agreement, must be completed and signed by the applicant, the agent and the lender, or by the applicant, the agent and the CDC on a 504 loan. Each agent needs a separate form, and an agent who fails to complete it risks suspension or revocation of the privilege to do business with SBA.\[3,13\]


-


**Tell the borrower an agent is optional.** Lenders, CDCs and agents must clearly inform applicants that SBA does not require the use of an agent for packaging or referring a loan application.\[3\]


-


**Expect to show your authority.** SBA will not discuss a loan with someone claiming to be an agent without evidence of representation, and may ask for it in writing.\[3\]


SBA also sets rules on what agents may charge and how. They are in the same chapter of the SOP, and worth reading in full before you agree terms with a borrower or lender.\[3\]

## Frequently asked questions


### What documents are required for an SBA 7(a) loan?


Under SOP 50 10 8.1, a 7(a) file includes SBA Form 1919 for the applicant and each co-borrower, a personal financial statement for every owner of 20% or more and each guarantor dated within 90 days, three years of business financial statements or tax returns with a debt schedule, an interim statement dated within 120 days, the same for affiliates, IRS Form 4506-C or 8821 for tax transcripts, and documents for the use of proceeds such as quotes, leases, purchase agreements and appraisals. Acquisitions and refinances need more. The lender may ask for anything else it needs to make a credit decision.


### What is in an SBA 504 loan application?


A 504 application is built around SBA Form 1244, which the borrower and the Certified Development Company complete together. It also needs the project cost documents, an appraisal of project real estate where required, the Third Party Lender’s letter of intent or term sheet stating why it will not finance the whole project, personal financial statements and one year of personal tax returns for owners of 20% or more, three years of business statements and returns, a recent interim with receivable and payable agings, a debt schedule, a schedule of previous government financing, and IRS Form 4506-C or 8821.


### What is the difference between packaging a 7(a) loan and a 504 loan?


A 7(a) loan is made by one lender and SBA guarantees part of it, so the package goes to that lender on SBA Form 1919. A 504 loan finances fixed assets through a Certified Development Company and a private Third Party Lender, so the package goes to the CDC on SBA Form 1244 and needs the Third Party Lender’s commitment. A 504 project also has to meet job creation or public policy goals and occupancy rules, and cannot fund working capital or inventory.


### Does a loan broker or packager have to sign SBA Form 159?


Yes, when you act as an agent on the loan. SBA’s SOP 50 10 8.1 says that for agents other than lender service providers working under an SBA-reviewed agreement, Form 159, the Fee Disclosure and Compensation Agreement, must be completed and signed by the applicant, the agent and the lender, or the CDC for a 504 loan. Each agent needs its own form. Failure to complete it can lead SBA to suspend or revoke the agent’s privilege to do business with SBA.


### Does a borrower need a packager to get an SBA loan?


No. SBA does not require the use of an agent for packaging or referring a loan application, and its procedures require lenders, CDCs and agents to tell applicants so. Borrowers use packagers because a complete, consistent file is a lot of work, not because SBA asks for one.


### Why do SBA loan packages stall?


The usual causes are documents that go stale before submission, financials that do not reconcile with IRS transcripts, ownership that does not add up to 100% or includes an ineligible owner, a debt schedule that leaves out shareholder or other debt, add-backs without support, an equity injection that cannot be traced through bank records, and for acquisitions a valuation that was not ordered by the lender.
